html:
SMTO-EXE-0183 — A file with that name already exists

GUID: 9527da80-6759-5485-8c57-38f836fbc385
Slug: office-output-conflict
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: office

What happened

  • SMTO always saves its result as a new file, and a file with the chosen name is already in that folder. SMTO never replaces an existing file, so nothing was overwritten.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open the file that already has that name and check whether it is the result of an earlier attempt of this same step. If an earlier attempt already saved what you wanted, you don't need to do the step again.
  2. If you still need the new version, ask SMTO to save it under a different file name, for example by adding "v2" or today's date. SMTO only saves to a name that isn't taken, so it never overwrites your files.
  3. Or ask SMTO to save the result without naming a folder, so it appears under Artifacts in SMTO's reply. Files saved there get a unique name automatically, so they can't clash with existing files.

What success looks like

  • SMTO reports the new file it created, and your existing file is unchanged.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with the file name and folder, to the person who manages SMTO. Don't delete the existing file just to make room until you've checked what is in it.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Office output publication was refused because the destination path already exists (file or symlink) or atomic create reported already_exists; Office never overwrites existing files, including the source.

What this means

  • Output publication found an existing file/symlink or received an already-exists result from atomic File creation. The Office path never overwrites the original or another existing destination. Office workers treat document content as untrusted data and never execute macros or formulas. Publication creates a separate output under existing File policy; retain revision and effect facts before any new write.

Why this can happen

  • Output publication found an existing file/symlink or received an already-exists result from atomic File creation. The Office path never overwrites the original or another existing destination.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the existing destination and original operation receipt before deciding whether it is an earlier successful output or unrelated content.

How to fix it

  • Choose an output_path that does not exist on the selected Gateway, or omit output_path so the result is published as a new run artifact with a unique prefix. Before choosing, check whether the existing file is the output of an earlier attempt of the same operation.
  • Choose a new output path. Office never overwrites an existing file, including the source.

Retry and execution caution

  • Choose a new output path. Office never overwrites an existing file, including the source.

How to verify the fix

  • A deliberately chosen new destination is used only for work still required.

What not to do

  • Never automatically replay uncertain writes or execute embedded document content.

Technical notes

  • Office workers treat document content as untrusted data and never execute macros or formulas. Publication creates a separate output under existing File policy; retain revision and effect facts before any new write.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
